summaryJa: 文書は1952年7月2日の未確認飛行物体（UFO）目撃に関する複数の米空軍報告をまとめたもので、主な内容は次の通り。アリゾナ州フェニックス：観察者はMrs. Arthur Wolfで、0420に約3～4分間、直径約7インチの炎の球と約8フィートの尾を引く光を地上から視認。音や既知飛行物に類する光はなく、物体は北西から現れて弧を描き南西へ移動、仰角は40°→30°→15°、距離推定7～10マイル。現地推定では南西で地面に接触した可能性があり捜索が要請されたが、航空機や気球の報告はなく（散布機の可能性が挙げられている）。ユタ州トレモントン：CPO Delbert C. Newhouse（海軍写真経験者）と家族が複数の光体を観察・35mmフィルムで撮影。写真は原本の35mmロールで、Wright FieldのPhoto Reconnaissance Laboratoryによる分析の写しが添付されている。ATIAA-5はこれらの映像を鳥類学者に照会すること（飛行中の鳥の可能性を検討）を提言している。気象は晴朗、太陽はほぼ頭上で観測条件良好、観察中に音や排気痕は記録されていない。
summaryEn: The documents compile USAF reports on unidentified aerial sightings of 2 July 1952. Phoenix, Arizona: Observer Mrs. Arthur Wolf reported at 0420 a glowing ball about seven inches across with an eight-foot tail, seen visually from the ground for 3–4 minutes with no sound or lights characteristic of known aircraft. The object appeared northwest of 1717 North 1st Ave, traced an arc to the southwest, with elevation angles roughly 40° (NW), 30° (W), 15° (SW) and an estimated range of 7–10 miles; it was presumed to have contacted the ground southwest of Phoenix and a search was requested. No aircraft or balloons were reported; crop-dusters were noted as a possibility. Tremonton, Utah: CPO Delbert C. Newhouse and family photographed multiple bright objects on 35mm film; the original roll is enclosed and a photostatic copy of an analysis by the Photo Reconnaissance Laboratory (Wright Field) is included. ATIAA-5 recommended submitting the film to an ornithologist (e.g., Smithsonian) to evaluate whether the objects could be birds. Weather was clear with the sun nearly overhead; observers reported no exhaust trails and no audible noise during observations.
